# **1\. Purpose and how to read this document**

This document describes what the CSS platform is used for, expressed as the goals its users pursue rather than the screens they pass through. It sits between the business requirements, which state why the platform exists, and the functional requirements, which state how each screen behaves.

Each use case names a primary actor, the goal that actor is trying to reach, the conditions that must hold before and after, and the sequence of steps that gets there. Alternative flows describe the paths that still reach the goal by another route; exceptions describe the paths that do not.

**Structure of a specification**

* Primary actor — the party whose goal the use case serves.

* Other participants — parties involved without owning the goal, including the system itself where it acts on its own.

* Trigger — the event that starts the use case.

* Preconditions — what must be true beforehand; if any fails, the use case cannot start.

* Postconditions — the state of the system once the use case has finished successfully.

* Covers — the functional requirement identifiers the use case realises, for tracing in both directions.

*Relationships between use cases follow the usual convention: «include» marks a step that always happens as part of the parent, and «extend» marks behaviour that happens only under a condition.*

# **2\. Actors**

An actor is a role rather than a person. One employee may act as several actors, and the permission matrix decides which of them a given account may be.

| Actor | Type | Interest in the system |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Manufacturer | Primary | Publishes and maintains a product catalog; sets list prices and dealer discounts; confirms purchase orders |
| Vendor | Primary | Buys from manufacturers and sells to restaurants; issues quotations, orders and invoices |
| Salesperson | Primary | A vendor employee who owns particular quotations and orders |
| Vendor manager | Primary | Approves assembly, adjusts order contents and confirms delivery |
| Packer | Primary | Assembles an order against the packing slip |
| Driver | Primary | Transports the order and records pick-up, arrival and delivery |
| Restaurant buyer | Primary | Places orders and requests quotations on behalf of an F\&B client |
| Restaurant client (F\&B client) | Primary | The buying company; reviews and signs quotations and receives goods |
| CSS administrator | Primary | Maintains the master database, subscribers, licences and reference data |
| Company owner | Primary | Registers a company by invitation code and completes onboarding |
| Buying group | Secondary | Recorded against a dealer; consolidates volume outside the platform |
| Manufacturer’s representative | Secondary | Represents a manufacturer in a territory; recorded on the manufacturer card |
| CSS AI Assistant | Secondary | Answers support questions and recognises data from uploaded invoices |
| Email service | Secondary | Delivers invitation codes, quotations and notifications |
| System (scheduler) | Secondary | Acts without a user: expires quotations, confirms orders on timeout, recalculates totals |

# **5\. Use case specifications**

## **5.1 Quotation**

**UC-01 — Create a quotation for a client**

| Primary actor | Vendor, salesperson |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Other participants** | F\&B client (as the subject of the quotation) |
| **Goal** | Open a priced offer against a named client, so that products can be added to it. |
| **Trigger** | The vendor clicks "+ Create new" from the quotations table, the vendor navigation, the manufacturer catalog or their own catalog. |
| **Preconditions** | The user is signed in with the right to create quotations. The client either exists in the database or will be entered manually. |
| **Postconditions** | A quotation exists in Draft status with a unique identifier, a name, a number and a client attached. The user remains on the page they started from. |
| **Covers** | FR-QUO-029 to FR-QUO-055 |

**Main flow**

1\.  The user opens the creation modal from one of the four entry points.

2\.  The system generates the quotation number from the configured numbering rules and offers it for editing.

3\.  The user enters the quotation name.

4\.  The user selects an existing client from the searchable list; the system populates the client identifier and name.

5\.  The user submits the form.

6\.  The system creates the quotation in Draft status, closes the modal and leaves the user where they were.

**Alternative flows**

**The client is not in the database**

* The user ticks "Client is not in the system"; the dropdown is replaced by the manual fields.

* The user enters the client name, contact person, email, phone number and address.

* The system validates the email and applies the phone mask for the selected country.

* On submission the system runs duplicate detection before creating the record.

**The user is a manufacturer rather than a vendor**

* The modal is titled "Choose Vendor", the list queries vendors, and the checkbox and address labels change accordingly.

**The user changes their mind mid-entry**

* Unticking the checkbox hides the manual fields but preserves what was typed, so nothing is lost if it is ticked again.

**Exceptions**

* A partial duplicate on name, phone or address opens the duplicate warning modal; Skip returns to the form, Proceed creates the record anyway.

* An exact duplicate violating a unique constraint disables submission and shows inline errors.

* Where the client list cannot be loaded, the system offers manual entry instead.

**UC-02 — Add products to a quotation**

| Primary actor | Vendor |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Other participants** | Manufacturer (as catalog owner) |
| **Goal** | Assemble the goods being offered, from one or more catalogs, into the quotation. |
| **Trigger** | The vendor opens a manufacturer catalog, their own catalog, or uses "+ Add Product" on the quotation. |
| **Preconditions** | A quotation exists in an editable state. |
| **Postconditions** | The quotation holds the selected products, grouped by manufacturer or vendor catalog, each with a captured price. |
| **Covers** | FR-QUO-118 to FR-QUO-155 |

**Main flow**

1\.  The vendor selects the quotation as the active context, or creates one from the catalog.

2\.  The vendor browses or searches the catalog and sets a quantity on a product.

3\.  The system adds the product to the quotation and confirms it on the product card.

4\.  The system captures the price at that moment, so that later catalog changes do not alter the quotation.

5\.  The vendor repeats this for further products, including products from other manufacturers.

**Alternative flows**

**No active context**

* The system intercepts the action, highlights the context area and asks the user to select an existing quotation or create a new one.

* A quotation created here becomes the active context automatically and the pending product is added.

**A new manufacturer group is needed**

* The vendor uses "+ Add product from new manufacturer / vendor catalog" and chooses the source; a new group is added to the quotation.

* A manufacturer already present is greyed out and cannot be chosen twice.

**Exceptions**

* Reducing a quantity to zero removes the line entirely rather than leaving a zero-quantity row.

* Where the active quotation has been deleted elsewhere, the system clears the context and asks for a valid one.

* A network failure during synchronisation reverts the stepper and reports that the update failed.

**UC-03 — Price a quotation**

| Primary actor | Vendor |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Other participants** | System (calculation) |
| **Goal** | Set the margin the vendor will earn and arrive at the price the client will see. |
| **Trigger** | The vendor edits a quantity, discount, markup or fee on the quotation page. |
| **Preconditions** | The quotation holds at least one product and is in Draft status. |
| **Postconditions** | Every line and the document totals are consistent, and the gross profit is known. |
| **Covers** | FR-QUO-060 to FR-QUO-077 |

**Main flow**

1\.  The vendor reviews the list price and the net price carried from the manufacturer agreement.

2\.  The vendor applies a markup globally, per item or for this quotation only.

3\.  The system recalculates the net price, sell price, margin and line subtotal as each field loses focus.

4\.  The system recalculates the group subtotals, the global subtotal, tax, total and gross profit.

5\.  The vendor adjusts freight, credit, discount and additional discount in the Details section.

**Alternative flows**

**Loss-leader pricing**

* Where a discount pushes the sell price below the net price, the margin turns negative and is highlighted, but the entry is allowed.

**Discount as a percentage or a flat amount**

* The $ and % toggle changes how the entered number is interpreted, and the total updates accordingly.

**Exceptions**

* Non-numeric input in a numeric field is rejected and the previous value restored.

* Where all products are removed, the totals reset to zero and conversion to an invoice is blocked.

* Where another user changes a catalog price while the draft is open, the draft keeps its captured price until it is refreshed.

**UC-04 — Configure what the client sees**

| Primary actor | Vendor |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Other participants** | F\&B client (as recipient) |
| **Goal** | Decide which pricing information leaves the company with the quotation. |
| **Trigger** | The vendor opens the Client View tab or the preview screen. |
| **Preconditions** | A quotation exists with at least one product. |
| **Postconditions** | The chosen visibility applies to the on-screen table, the preview, the print, the export and the document sent to the client. |
| **Covers** | FR-QUO-078 to FR-QUO-098 |

**Main flow**

1\.  The vendor switches to Client View and sees the internal columns disappear.

2\.  The vendor sets the Preview Settings: list price, sell price, discount, or no pricing at all.

3\.  The system applies the choice to the products table immediately.

4\.  The vendor previews the document as the client will receive it.

**Alternative flows**

**Sending without prices**

* Selecting "Without Price" clears the three price checkboxes and suppresses the subtotal column and the financial totals on the client document.

* Selecting any price checkbox afterwards clears "Without Price" again.

**Exceptions**

* Where the settings cannot be saved because of a network error, the system warns before an export or a send is attempted.

* Hiding a column never changes the underlying arithmetic; the totals remain correct on the vendor side.

**UC-05 — Send a quotation to a client**

| Primary actor | Vendor |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Other participants** | Email service, F\&B client |
| **Goal** | Put the finished quotation in front of the client and start the validity clock. |
| **Trigger** | The vendor presses Send on the preview screen. |
| **Preconditions** | The quotation is complete and the client has an email address on file, unless only printing is chosen. |
| **Postconditions** | The quotation status is Sent, the validity date is active, and the client has received the document. |
| **Covers** | FR-QUO-099 to FR-QUO-117 |

**Main flow**

1\.  The system pre-fills the client email address and calculates the Valid Until date as 30 days from the quotation date.

2\.  The vendor confirms or changes the delivery options and the validity date.

3\.  The vendor presses Send.

4\.  The system generates the PDF from the previewed layout, sends it using the standard template, and moves the status from Draft to Sent.

**Alternative flows**

**Printing instead of emailing**

* With Print on, the system opens the printable PDF in a new browser tab as well as, or instead of, sending it.

**Exceptions**

* With both delivery methods off, submission is blocked with a prompt to choose one.

* A validity date in the past raises an inline error.

* Where the email service fails, the modal stays open, an error is shown and the status remains Draft.

* Where the browser blocks the print tab, the system suggests allowing pop-ups or downloading the PDF.

**UC-06 — Respond to a received quotation**

| Primary actor | F\&B client |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Other participants** | Vendor |
| **Goal** | Accept the offer, or send it back with the changes the restaurant needs. |
| **Trigger** | The client opens a quotation in the Received tab. |
| **Preconditions** | A quotation has been sent to the client and has not expired. |
| **Postconditions** | Either an order exists and the quotation is Accepted, or the vendor holds a modification request. |
| **Covers** | FR-QUO-156 to FR-QUO-180 |

**Main flow**

1\.  The client opens the quotation; the badge count of unopened quotations decreases.

2\.  The client reviews the flat list of products and the totals; all core information is read-only.

3\.  The client ticks the agreement checkbox and signs the quotation.

4\.  The system converts the quotation into an order, sets the status to Accepted and records the acceptance, the customer name and the timestamp.

**Alternative flows**

**The client needs changes**

* The client edits the ordered quantity or removes a line; signing becomes unavailable.

* The client uses "Request modifications" to send the quotation back to the vendor for a revised version.

**The client wants a fresh price on an expired quotation**

* The client duplicates an expired quotation, which asks the vendor to refresh it rather than creating a new quotation from scratch.

**Exceptions**

* Where the vendor converts the quotation to an order at the same moment, the modification request is aborted and the client is told the quotation has already been converted.

* Where signing fails, the agreement checkbox stays ticked and the client is asked to retry or contact the vendor.

* A quantity increase or a new product requires vendor confirmation and therefore blocks signing.

**UC-07 — Expire a quotation**

| Primary actor | System (scheduler) |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Other participants** | Vendor, F\&B client |
| **Goal** | Close off quotations that have gone unanswered, so that the pipeline reflects reality. |
| **Trigger** | The validity date passes without a client response. |
| **Preconditions** | The quotation is in Sent status and carries a validity date. |
| **Postconditions** | The quotation is in Over 30 Days status and appears in that tab for both parties. |
| **Covers** | FR-QUO-008, FR-QUO-010, FR-QUO-163 |

**Main flow**

1\.  The system compares the current date with the quotation’s validity date.

2\.  Where no acceptance or modification request has been recorded, the status changes automatically.

**Alternative flows**

**No validity date was supplied**

* On the client side the 30 days are counted from the date the quotation was received instead.

**A custom validity period was set**

* Expiry follows the date the vendor entered rather than a fixed 30-day timer.

## **5.2 Catalog and import**

**UC-08 — Load a catalog in bulk**

| Primary actor | Manufacturer |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Other participants** | CSS administrator, system (parser) |
| **Goal** | Get a whole product range into the platform without typing it in. |
| **Trigger** | The user starts the import wizard from the catalog. |
| **Preconditions** | The user holds write access to that catalog. The source data is in a supported format. |
| **Postconditions** | The catalog holds the imported products, a new version exists and the import is recorded in the audit log. |
| **Covers** | FR-CAT-009 to FR-CAT-016, FR-CAT-039 to FR-CAT-045 |

**Main flow**

1\.  The user chooses the import method: a file, pasted tabular data, or manual entry.

2\.  The user uploads the file; the system parses it and reports the rows and columns recognised.

3\.  The user maps the columns (UC-09) and the system validates the data (UC-10).

4\.  The user confirms; the system writes the records asynchronously and reports what was added, updated and skipped.

**Alternative flows**

**Pasting rather than uploading**

* The user pastes rows copied from a spreadsheet; the same mapping and validation follow, and the data can be edited before processing.

**Reusing a previous mapping**

* The user loads a saved mapping profile, and the manual mapping step is skipped.

**Exceptions**

* A file whose structure cannot be read stops the import with a request to reformat it or paste the data instead.

* A file with headers but no data rows leaves the continue control inactive.

* A PDF is not processed by the wizard; the request is passed to a manual process.

**UC-09 — Map source columns to system fields**

| Primary actor | Manufacturer |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Other participants** | System (suggestion engine) |
| **Goal** | Tell the platform what each column of the source file means. |
| **Trigger** | The wizard reaches the mapping step. |
| **Preconditions** | A file or pasted block has been parsed and its headers are known. |
| **Postconditions** | Every required field is mapped, and the mapping may be saved for reuse. |
| **Covers** | FR-CAT-017 to FR-CAT-028 |

**Main flow**

1\.  The system proposes a mapping for each column from header similarity and previous mappings.

2\.  The user reviews the proposals and overrides any of them.

3\.  The user excludes the columns that should not be imported.

4\.  The user optionally saves the configuration as a named profile.

**Alternative flows**

**Attributes hidden in free text**

* Where a description or notes column is mapped, the system extracts technical attributes from it and shows them in the preview.

**Exceptions**

* A required field left unmapped blocks the import and the column is highlighted.

* Mapping two columns to the same field is refused.

* New system fields cannot be created during mapping.

**UC-10 — Correct rejected rows**

| Primary actor | Manufacturer |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Other participants** | System (validation) |
| **Goal** | Get the rows that failed validation into the catalog without editing the original file. |
| **Trigger** | Validation reports errors, or mandatory values are missing. |
| **Preconditions** | The mapping is complete and the data has been checked. |
| **Postconditions** | Either the corrected rows are imported, or the user has a report describing what to fix. |
| **Covers** | FR-CAT-029 to FR-CAT-038 |

**Main flow**

1\.  The system lists the rows that failed, marking the cell and the rule broken.

2\.  The user corrects values inline, or fills missing mandatory values in bulk through "Add missing information".

3\.  The user reruns the validation and confirms the import.

**Alternative flows**

**Fixing the data offline**

* The user downloads the error report, which names the row, the field and the violation, corrects the source and starts again.

**Exceptions**

* Values entered during the wizard apply to this import only and never modify the source file.

* A child variation without a valid parent blocks the import.

**UC-11 — Maintain a single product**

| Primary actor | Manufacturer |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Other participants** | Vendor, restaurant client (as readers) |
| **Goal** | Create or correct one product without running an import. |
| **Trigger** | The user opens the new product form or an existing product card. |
| **Preconditions** | The catalog exists and the user holds write access. |
| **Postconditions** | The product is created or updated, a new version entry exists and the audit log records the change. |
| **Covers** | FR-CAT-046 to FR-CAT-049, FR-CAT-006 |

**Main flow**

1\.  The user opens the product form and completes the required fields.

2\.  The system applies the same constraints as an import, including the description length limits.

3\.  The user saves; the version history and the audit log update immediately.

**Exceptions**

* Required fields left empty prevent submission.

**UC-12 — Take over catalog ownership**

| Primary actor | Manufacturer |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Other participants** | CSS administrator |
| **Goal** | Move from CSS maintaining the catalog to the manufacturer maintaining it. |
| **Trigger** | CSS completes the initial catalog setup and hands it over. |
| **Preconditions** | A catalog exists at version 1.0 and the manufacturer holds an account. |
| **Postconditions** | The manufacturer can add, edit and delete its own products; other manufacturers’ catalogs remain unreachable. |
| **Covers** | FR-CAT-007, FR-CAT-008 |

**Main flow**

1\.  CSS creates the catalog and version 1.0 is recorded.

2\.  Write access is granted to the manufacturer’s account.

3\.  The manufacturer signs in and modifies a product to verify the handover.

4\.  Each subsequent manufacturer update increments the catalog version.

**Exceptions**

* An attempt to reach another manufacturer’s catalog or mapping profiles is refused.

## **5.3 Platform administration**

**UC-13 — Onboard a new subscriber**

| Primary actor | CSS administrator |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Other participants** | Email service, company owner |
| **Goal** | Create a company record and give its owner a way to register. |
| **Trigger** | The administrator presses "+ Add new" in the subscriber table. |
| **Preconditions** | The administrator holds the right to create clients. |
| **Postconditions** | A company exists with NOT SUBSCRIBED status and a unique invitation code has been emailed to it. |
| **Covers** | FR-ADM-099 to FR-ADM-108 |

**Main flow**

1\.  The administrator completes the type, client name, phone number, email and address, and optionally the number of licence seats.

2\.  The administrator presses Send Code.

3\.  The system validates the fields, checks the email for duplicates and generates a unique code.

4\.  The system creates the company, sends the code to the address given and confirms the send.

**Alternative flows**

**Abandoning the form**

* Cancelling with fields filled raises a discard warning; no code is generated, so nothing is consumed.

**Exceptions**

* An email address already in the system blocks creation and no code is generated.

* An invalid phone format for the selected country blocks submission.

**UC-14 — Register a company by invitation code**

| Primary actor | Company owner |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Other participants** | CSS administrator, system |
| **Goal** | Turn an invitation into a working account and an active subscription. |
| **Trigger** | The owner opens the sign-up screen and enters the code received by email. |
| **Preconditions** | A company exists with an unused invitation code. |
| **Postconditions** | The company is ACTIVE, the code is Used, the subscription dates are set from the actual registration, and the company appears in the subscriber table. |
| **Covers** | FR-ADM-093, FR-AUT-001 to FR-AUT-035 |

**Main flow**

1\.  The owner enters the invitation code, which is validated as it is typed.

2\.  The owner sets a password meeting the complexity rules and completes the profile fields.

3\.  The owner chooses the business type, which determines whether restaurant or store attributes are collected.

4\.  The owner completes the company and core team screens; the first participant is the Owner by default.

5\.  The system activates the company, marks the code Used, overwrites the activation date with the registration date, recalculates the expiration date and notifies the administrator to verify the dates.

**Alternative flows**

**The core team form is incomplete**

* At least the Owner participant is saved, and the missing fields are marked inline.

**Exceptions**

* An unknown code is refused as soon as it is entered.

* A password failing the complexity rules cannot be submitted.

**UC-15 — Merge duplicate companies**

| Primary actor | CSS administrator |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Other participants** | System |
| **Goal** | Reduce several records describing one company to a single correct record. |
| **Trigger** | The administrator selects two or more companies and presses Merge. |
| **Preconditions** | Every selected company shares one company type. |
| **Postconditions** | One master record holds the resolved data; the subordinate records are deleted. |
| **Covers** | FR-ADM-034 to FR-ADM-048 |

**Main flow**

1\.  The administrator reviews the chosen companies and removes any that do not belong.

2\.  The administrator designates the master record.

3\.  The system checks the subordinates for exact duplicates and offers to skip them or merge anyway.

4\.  The system compares every field of the company card and presents the differences.

5\.  The administrator resolves each conflict: replace, add or ignore, according to whether the field holds one value or several.

6\.  The system updates the master record, deletes the subordinates and reports the result.

**Alternative flows**

**Removing the designated master**

* The master selection is cleared and has to be made again.

**Exceptions**

* Selecting companies of different types stops the merge with an explanatory message.

* Reducing the scope to one company blocks the merge, which needs at least two.

* A subordinate with ACTIVE or EXPIRED status is deleted as an explicit exception to the deletion rule.

**UC-16 — Delete companies in bulk**

| Primary actor | CSS administrator |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Other participants** | System |
| **Goal** | Remove records that carry no commercial history, without touching those that do. |
| **Trigger** | The administrator selects rows in the master database and presses Delete. |
| **Preconditions** | The administrator is working in the master database, where the control is available. |
| **Postconditions** | Only companies with NOT SUBSCRIBED status have been removed; the rest are untouched and reported. |
| **Covers** | FR-ADM-049 to FR-ADM-057 |

**Main flow**

1\.  The system checks the status of every selected record.

2\.  Where all are deletable, a confirmation is shown and the records are removed.

3\.  The system reports how many were deleted.

**Alternative flows**

**A mixed selection**

* The system reports how many will be deleted and how many cannot, listing each with its status, and deletes only the permitted ones.

**Exceptions**

* Where every selected record is protected, a banner explains that a registered company cannot be deleted and nothing is removed.

* The delete control is not offered in the subscriber table at all.

**UC-17 — Change a company type**

| Primary actor | CSS administrator |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Other participants** | System (validation) |
| **Goal** | Correct the type of a company recorded wrongly, without breaking the business model. |
| **Trigger** | The administrator changes the type on the company card or through bulk edit and saves. |
| **Preconditions** | The company holds nothing beyond the general information created at onboarding. |
| **Postconditions** | Either the type is changed, or it is unchanged and the blocking records are named. |
| **Covers** | FR-ADM-118 to FR-ADM-131 |

**Main flow**

1\.  The administrator selects a different company type and saves.

2\.  The system checks for clients, products, invoices, orders, type-specific teams and B2B relations.

3\.  Where none exist, the change is saved and confirmed.

**Alternative flows**

**The company has subsidiaries**

* The system asks whether to detach the subsidiaries or change their type as well.

**The blocking data has since been removed**

* Once the counts are zero the change is permitted again.

**Exceptions**

* Where any blocking record exists, the save is rejected and the message names the categories found.

* No data is migrated or silently deleted to make the change possible.

* Where a blocking record appears while the form is open, the validation inside the saving transaction still refuses the change.

**UC-18 — Manage a subscription and its licences**

| Primary actor | CSS administrator |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Other participants** | System |
| **Goal** | Keep the commercial terms of a subscriber current: seats, dates, fee and payment. |
| **Trigger** | The administrator opens the Subscription tab of a company card. |
| **Preconditions** | The company exists; it may or may not already be a subscriber. |
| **Postconditions** | The subscription data is stored, the dates are consistent and the licence events are logged. |
| **Covers** | FR-ADM-073 to FR-ADM-097 |

**Main flow**

1\.  The administrator enters the received date; the system sets the activation date and calculates the expiration date from the billing period.

2\.  The administrator sets the licence count, the fee, the paid amount and the payment method.

3\.  The administrator saves; the licence events are written to the Licenses tab and the other changes to History.

**Alternative flows**

**Reducing the licence count below the seats in use**

* The change is stored, and the system explains that it takes effect after the subscription expires; the remaining seats keep showing the previous figure until then.

**Changing the billing period on a running subscription**

* The system asks whether to recalculate the dates now or to apply the new period after the current one ends.

**Adding a payment method that is not on the list**

* A new method is created and becomes available to every administrator.

**Exceptions**

* An expiration date earlier than the activation date is refused with an inline error.

* Completing this tab does not activate a subscription; only registration by invitation code does.

## **5.4 Order fulfilment**

**UC-19 — Confirm an order as the vendor**

| Primary actor | Vendor manager |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Other participants** | Restaurant buyer, system |
| **Goal** | Accept an incoming order for what can actually be supplied, at the right price. |
| **Trigger** | A new order arrives and the vendor opens it from the orders list. |
| **Preconditions** | An order exists in New status against this vendor. |
| **Postconditions** | The order is confirmed with the agreed contents, and the restaurant has been notified. |
| **Covers** | FR-RST-043 to FR-RST-053 |

**Main flow**

1\.  The vendor opens the order and reviews the customer, payment and delivery information.

2\.  The system highlights any line whose ordered quantity exceeds available stock.

3\.  The vendor confirms availability or adjusts the vendor quantity, and may change prices, taxes and the delivery fee.

4\.  The vendor removes or adds products as needed.

5\.  The vendor confirms the order; the system saves the changes, sets the status to confirmed and notifies the restaurant.

**Alternative flows**

**Changing the delivery slot**

* The vendor selects a new date and time from its declared delivery days and windows.

**Talking to the client first**

* The vendor opens the chat with the responsible restaurant contact from the same screen.

**Exceptions**

* Cancelling the order cancels it in full, notifies the restaurant and returns the vendor to the list.

**UC-20 — Assemble an order**

| Primary actor | Packer |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Other participants** | Vendor manager |
| **Goal** | Pick and pack the goods against the packing slip and hand them over for delivery. |
| **Trigger** | A confirmed order reaches the warehouse. |
| **Preconditions** | A packing slip exists for the order. |
| **Postconditions** | The packing slip is PACKED and the order is ready to ship. |
| **Covers** | FR-VND-095 to FR-VND-101 |

**Main flow**

1\.  The packer opens the packing slip and works through the product lines.

2\.  The packer marks each product packed.

3\.  Once every line is marked, the packer presses Ready to Ship and the slip moves to PACKED.

**Alternative flows**

**Short shipment**

* The shipped quantity is reduced; the back order value is the ordered quantity less the shipped quantity.

**Manager assembly**

* Where the manager packs the order, Approve or Ready to Ship moves it from NEW to PACKED depending on whether manager approval is required.

**Exceptions**

* A problem with a product is reported through "Report a problem", which opens a message to the manager.

**UC-21 — Deliver an order**

| Primary actor | Driver |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Other participants** | F\&B client, vendor manager |
| **Goal** | Move the goods to the restaurant and record that they arrived and were accepted. |
| **Trigger** | A packed order is assigned for delivery. |
| **Preconditions** | The packing slip is in PACKED status. |
| **Postconditions** | The order is DELIVERED and the timeline records the pick-up and delivery times. |
| **Covers** | FR-VND-098, FR-VND-030 |

**Main flow**

1\.  The driver presses Pick Up; the status becomes ON THE WAY and the pick-up time is recorded.

2\.  The driver delivers the goods and presses Arrived; the status becomes ARRIVED.

3\.  The client accepts the goods and the driver presses Confirm Delivery; the status becomes DELIVERED.

**Exceptions**

* Where the manager records delivery instead, the same transitions apply from the order card.

**UC-22 — Issue an invoice and record payment**

| Primary actor | Vendor |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Other participants** | F\&B client |
| **Goal** | Bill the client for a delivered order and keep the balance current. |
| **Trigger** | The vendor uses Generate Invoice on an order, or opens an issued invoice. |
| **Preconditions** | An order exists with agreed contents and prices. |
| **Postconditions** | An invoice exists with a number issued under the configured numbering rules, and payments are recorded against it. |
| **Covers** | FR-VND-085 to FR-VND-094, FR-VND-102 |

**Main flow**

1\.  The vendor generates the invoice from the order; the number is produced from the numbering settings.

2\.  The invoice appears in the order documents and in the issued invoices list.

3\.  The vendor opens the invoice and records a payment: amount, method, date and an optional reference.

4\.  The system updates the paid amount and the balance due.

**Alternative flows**

**Several invoices on one day**

* The same-day rule appends a sequence number after a slash, or increments the base number, depending on the setting.

**Marking an invoice fully paid**

* The Invoice Paid toggle settles the balance without recording a separate payment line.

**Exceptions**

* The invoice cannot be generated where the order holds no products.

## **5.5 Restaurant ordering**

**UC-23 — Place an order with a vendor**

| Primary actor | Restaurant buyer |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Other participants** | Vendor |
| **Goal** | Buy what the restaurant needs, at a price the buyer can compare against previous purchases. |
| **Trigger** | The buyer presses Create Order, or starts from the empty state on the orders page. |
| **Preconditions** | The restaurant is registered and at least one vendor is reachable. |
| **Postconditions** | An order exists against the chosen vendor with the requested delivery date, awaiting vendor confirmation. |
| **Covers** | FR-RST-028 to FR-RST-042 |

**Main flow**

1\.  The buyer chooses a vendor from Your Vendors, or searches All Vendors by name, type or location.

2\.  The buyer browses the vendor catalog, comparing current prices against a chosen earlier period.

3\.  The buyer sets quantities; the running total appears at the foot of the page.

4\.  The buyer chooses the payment method and a delivery date and time within the vendor’s declared windows.

5\.  The buyer reviews the order and submits it.

**Alternative flows**

**No orders yet**

* The empty state offers Choose Vendor with the full vendor list expanded.

**No existing relationship with any vendor**

* Where Your Vendors is empty, the buyer can invite a vendor to the platform.

**Repeating a previous purchase**

* The buyer duplicates an earlier order rather than rebuilding the basket.

**Exceptions**

* Dates in the past cannot be chosen.

* An address beyond the vendor’s maximum delivery distance cannot be used, or requires a separately calculated cost.

**UC-24 — Respond to vendor changes**

| Primary actor | Restaurant buyer |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Other participants** | Vendor, system (timer) |
| **Goal** | Accept or reject what the vendor changed while confirming the order. |
| **Trigger** | The vendor confirms the order having altered it. |
| **Preconditions** | The order was placed by this restaurant and confirmed with changes. |
| **Postconditions** | The order is either confirmed with the vendor’s changes or cancelled. |
| **Covers** | FR-RST-054 to FR-RST-059 |

**Main flow**

1\.  The buyer receives a notification and opens the order.

2\.  A warning block below the line items lists what the vendor changed and starts a 30-minute countdown.

3\.  The buyer confirms the order, accepting the changes.

**Alternative flows**

**Rejecting the changes**

* The buyer cancels the order from the warning block or from the foot of the page; both sets of controls behave identically.

**No response within the window**

* The order is confirmed automatically when the timer expires; cancellation remains possible from the order page under the normal rules.

**The vendor changed nothing**

* Only a confirmation notification is sent; no warning block and no timer appear.

**Exceptions**

* Order comments stay hidden until the order is confirmed.

**UC-25 — Maintain the manufacturer relationship**

| Primary actor | Vendor |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Other participants** | Manufacturer |
| **Goal** | Keep the commercial terms agreed with each manufacturer, without touching the manufacturer’s own data. |
| **Trigger** | The vendor opens a manufacturer card from MFR Contacts. |
| **Preconditions** | The manufacturer exists in the global directory. |
| **Postconditions** | The vendor’s discounts, terms, category pricing and representation details are stored privately against that manufacturer. |
| **Covers** | FR-MFR-001 to FR-MFR-042 |

**Main flow**

1\.  The vendor classifies the manufacturer as Preferred, Approved, Not Approved or Not Assigned; the status applies across the platform.

2\.  The vendor records the master discount, margin, cash terms, rebate, shipping level, preferred carrier and buying group.

3\.  The vendor records category-specific multipliers and margins as reference information.

4\.  The vendor records the representation agency, its MAFSI areas and its contacts.

5\.  The vendor saves; the manufacturer’s own data remains unchanged.

**Alternative flows**

**Reviewing the terms later**

* The list view shows the discount, representative, buying group, rebate and last transaction at a glance.

**Exceptions**

* Master data is read-only in the vendor view, and vendor pricing is invisible in the manufacturer view.

* Category multipliers do not affect quotation pricing at this stage.

# **6\. Points that affect more than one use case**

The items below are unresolved in the functional requirements and change the flow of the use cases named beside them. They are repeated here because a use case reads as settled even where the underlying decision is not.

| Point | What is undecided | Use cases affected |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Order status model | Two status sets, one with pending and one with On the Way and Arrived | UC-19, UC-20, UC-21, UC-23 |
| Total and line arithmetic | The grand total formula omits tax, GST and credit; the line subtotal is defined twice | UC-03, UC-22, UC-23 |
| Who confirms an order first | The status model says the buyer confirms; the flow has the vendor confirming and the buyer accepting changes | UC-19, UC-24 |
| Product identity | SKU within a catalog, or customer number with model number | UC-08, UC-09, UC-10 |
| PDF as an import source | Parsed by the wizard in one source, sent to a manual process in another | UC-08 |
| Invalid rows on import | Block the whole import, or import the valid rows | UC-10 |
| NOT SUBSCRIBED in the subscriber table | Three contradictory statements | UC-13, UC-16 |
| Convert to invoice permissions | Restricted to managers, or governed by an approval rule | UC-22 |
| Type change through bulk edit | Whether the blocking validation applies to the bulk path and to subsidiaries | UC-17 |
| Merging protected companies | Whether the licence and invoice history of deleted subordinates is carried into the master record | UC-15 |
